# iliad-073 (12.88–181): new recurring-formula renderings

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ἀμώμητος (Πουλυδάμας ἀμωμήτοιο, 12.109) | "faultless" | "faultless" | "blameless" (kept for ἀμύμων, whose meaning is not known), "flawless", "perfect" | ἀμώμητος is from μωμάομαι "find fault with", so "without fault"; kept apart from ἀμύμων "blameless" |
| ὑψικάρηνος (δρύες … ὑψικάρηνοι, 12.132) | "high-headed" | "high-headed" | "high-crowned" (kept for ὑψίκομος), "tall" (kept for μακρός), "lofty" | ὑψι- "high" + κάρηνον "head, top" |
| φιλοψευδής (Ζεῦ πάτερ … φιλοψευδὴς ἐτέτυξο, 12.164) | "lie-loving" | "fond of lies" | "deceitful", "a liar" | φιλο- "fond of" + ψεῦδος "lie" |
| βέλεα (ἐκ χειρῶν βέλεα ῥέον, 12.159) | "missiles" | "missiles" | "shafts" (the Iliad's usual βέλος) | departure from the Iliad's βέλος "shaft", following the 8.159 row (βέλεα στονόεντα "missiles"): stones and every thrown weapon are meant, as the neighbouring lines about stones show |
| σανίδες (ἐπικεκλιμένας σανίδας, 12.121) | "doors" | "doors" | "boards", "planks" | follows the Iliad's κολλητὰς σανίδας "close-joined doors" (9.583); the note says σανίς is literally "board" |
| ὀχεύς (μακρὸν ὀχῆα, 12.121) | "the long bar" | "the long bar" | "bolt", "clasp" (the Odyssey's ὀχῆες χρύσειοι "clasps" are a different object) | the gate-bar |
| μύλαξ (μυλάκεσσι, 12.161) | "millstones" | "great round stones" | "boulders" (kept for χερμάδιον in the table's refusal list), "rocks" | μύλαξ is a stone as big as a millstone; χερμάδιον stays "stone" |
| αὖον ἀΰτευν (12.160) | "rang dry" | "rang harshly" | "rang hollow", "shouted" | αὖος "dry", of a harsh sound |
| κολοσυρτός (12.147) | "uproar" | "uproar" | "tumult" (refused for Κυδοιμός), "rabble", "mob" | |
| δοχμώ (12.148) | "slantwise" | "slantwise" | "sideways", "aslant" | dual agreeing with the two boars |
| ἀλαστέω (ἀλαστήσας, 12.163) | "in bitter indignation" | "in bitter indignation" | "angrily" (anger is χόλος), "in rage" | root of ἄλαστος "not to be forgotten"; the exact force is not certain, and the note says so |
| σφῆκες μέσον αἰόλοι (12.167) | "wasps, in the middle quick-moving" | "wasps, nimble at the waist" | "bright-bodied", "glittering", "tawny" | αἰόλος "quick-moving, flashing", μέσον probably the waist; the note says the sense is not settled |
| ἐπιτάρροθος (12.180) | "helpers" | "helpers" | "champions", "protectors" | the Odyssey ships "helper" (24.182); rare word, note gives sense only |
| εἴσατο γὰρ νηῶν ἐπ’ ἀριστερά (12.118) | "made for the left of the ships" | "had gone to the left of the ships" | "seemed" | εἴσατο taken from ἵεμαι "rush", not εἴδομαι "seem" (see εἴσαντο at 12.103, "seemed") |
| σὺν δ’ ἔβαλον … πόλεμον καὶ δηϊοτῆτα (12.181) | "together they threw … war and fighting" | "joined war and fighting together" | "joined battle" (the idiom; the note gives it) | |

Departures from the Odyssey: none beyond the βέλεα and σανίδες rows above, which follow the Iliad's own table.

Reused from the table unchanged: ἐῢς πάϊς Ἀγχίσαο "the good son of Anchises", ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν "chief of men", θεοειδής "godlike in form", αἴθων "fire-bright", ἀγακλειτός "renowned", ἀρήϊος "warlike", τηλεκλειτοί "far-famed", ἠνεμόεσσα "windy", κῆρες "death-fates" / "fates of death", δυσώνυμος "ill-named", ἀγαυός "noble", βροτολοιγὸς Ἄρης, ἐΰδμητος "well-built", ἐϋκνήμιδες "well-greaved", θεσπιδαὲς πῦρ "wondrous-blazing fire", ζαής "hard-blowing", σκιόεντα "shadowy", πουλυβοτείρῃ "much-nourishing", ὀμφαλόεσσαι "bossed", ἀάπτους "untouchable" / "irresistible", κόμπος ὀδόντων "a din of teeth", ἀχνύμενοί περ "though grieving", ἀκαχήμενος "grieved", ὠκύπορος "swift-faring", παιπαλόεσσα "rugged".
